title: Balanced Confidence Calibration for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Confidence calibration is a challenge for Graph Neural Network predictions.

gap.claim: Existing calibration methods focus predominantly on the highest logit and neglect the full prediction-probability spectrum, while entropy minimization can cause over-confidence.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Balanced Calibrated Graph Neural Network framework to balance over-confidence and under-confidence in GNN predictions.
Demonstrates the mechanism by which BCGNN performs confidence calibration and improves prediction trustworthiness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe BCGNN as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments were conducted to examine BCGNN.
The authors report superior performance in predictive confidence and trustworthiness, supporting practical applicability and effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN confidence calibration is a notable challenge.
Entropy minimization seeks to increase confidence but risks over-confidence.
Existing methods mainly attend to the highest logit rather than the complete probability distribution.
BCGNN is introduced to balance over-confidence and under-confidence.
The framework is theoretically supported and evaluated through experiments with reported gains in confidence and trustworthiness.

source_observation.claim: Confidence calibration methods may overlook the full prediction-probability spectrum.

interpretation.claim: Calibration should account for the distribution of probabilities rather than only the top logit.

application.claim: When designing confidence calibration, evaluate and regulate the full predicted probability distribution.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this principle generalizes beyond GNN prediction calibration.

source_observation.claim: Increasing confidence through entropy minimization can produce over-confident predictions.

interpretation.claim: Confidence improvement requires balancing under-confidence against over-confidence.

application.claim: Assess confidence-enhancement methods for both increased confidence and calibration balance.

exception.claim: The abstract provides no conditions identifying when entropy minimization becomes over-confident.
